milestones.name: A repeatable offscreen valley proves the comparison path
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: One reproducible command drives the real cooked game through the existing moving route plus day/night and variant-switch coverage, writes full-resolution sequence and linear-image checkpoints, and records build, shader, cooked, route, recipe, viewport and generation identity.
items.inspect: Inspect the native offscreen sequence at 1x: Sun side, near/far valley, mirror/local-light checkpoint, pre/post cut and night. Check full frames and native-size crops for missing scene content. No physical cadence claim.
items.ask: Run the documented M0 command from its retained evidence. Does it refuse a missing/mismatched cooked root, log every submitted route sample and cut, expose local lights/mirrors, include both star and no-star variants and a switch, and preserve the G7 baseline/comparator? Are new fixture/tool commands implemented before being cited as checks?

items.statement: Two same-build native portable runs have byte-identical matching checkpoint images and complete route/sample identity. Retained full-resolution pre-change portable baselines, scene-linear readbacks and the mechanism-specific exactness contract in APPLE-TILE.md govern later changes; only the labelled native blend permits its separate 1-ULP f16 bound.
items.ask: Compare exact checkpoint hashes and linear readbacks, not coarse grids. Retain native pre-change portable images and provenance before M1, with fixed exposure/headroom, formats and complete sample accounting. Do phase mismatch, missing contribution, one dropped weak local light in an overflowing cluster, one omitted mirrored cube at overlay slot 5060 and the removed night star layer each fail the applicable per-pixel comparison? Show nonzero affected pixels/crops, including rejection under the native-blend bound when enabled. Keep same-target timing spread separate from image and display proof; do not widen tolerance or replace the baseline to pass.

items.statement: Opt-in generation-owned creation diagnostics retain pipeline events by thread/phase and reject an unscoped pipeline creation after readiness; default builds retain the direct creation seam and no diagnostic submit lock.
items.ask: Confirm production pipeline coverage, same-generation clones and detached preparation attribution. Keep live-object net deltas distinct from creation events; native-object instrumentation remains absent until a native producer exists.

items.statement: The retained Xcode replay probe establishes per-encoder device-memory byte measurement on this M3 Max; uncaptured rows stay unmeasured and logical attachment bytes stay separate.
items.ask: Read G3T-TRAFFIC-PROBE-2026-11-08.md: does it establish the actual counter and units, per-encoder rather than per-attachment attribution, one-replay/shared-load limits and unavailable raw scratch? No new replay or physical-traffic result is implied.

items.statement: Chrome portable runs the same cooked route twice with matching per-tick identity and repeat checkpoint images; it remains a functional portable consumer, with no native-display claim.
items.ask: Confirm this existing command is used as route/content smoke proof, not the finer G3t recipe image evaluator. Record any browser availability block without substituting a Wasm compile.

milestones.name: The valley selects a recipe and stores only actual future inputs
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: One generation registry resolves requested Apple tile on eligible Metal/unified-memory hardware, portable on Chrome and unsupported hardware, with a stable digest and validated force override. Platform shells capture once and passes never probe privately. The normal default remains portable until integrated paired evidence justifies promotion.
items.ask: Inspect selection tests for eligible/ineligible/unknown facts, forced portable, unsupported forced Apple and invalid override. Are enabled facts distinguished from offered features and display facts kept with the platform?

items.statement: Compiled prepared variants report attachment eligibility/reasons and actual Metal storage: render-only last-use transient attachments may be memoryless; explicit stores, star/occlusion/capture readers, histories, persistent/imported resources and later readers are stored.
items.ask: Run graph mutation tests: add a reader, explicit store, history/persistent use and capture-only read; verify only the affected variant changes and no normal-path usage is widened. Inspect a Texture::as_hal storage-mode log for Memoryless vs Private under both recipes. Report unique resident allocations/bytes under both recipes, including all prepared day/star/capture variants, fallback-only resources and old/new generation overlap. Verify no stored twin exists solely for a memoryless-only attachment override; whole-recipe changes prepare a new generation before publication.

items.statement: Both native recipes retain exact scene-linear and submitted SDR route bytes against paired and pre-change portable controls, with no validation errors or pipeline/texture creation when switching prepared variants.
items.inspect: Compare matched day/night frames and full-resolution motion sequences against portable, checking Sun, sky, stars, shadows, mirror and local light. Inspect creation events through a variant switch and the per-variant storage report. Reconcile the resident total and fallback-only bytes under both recipes with D1.2; simultaneous stored and memoryless variants count as separate allocations. A traffic reduction alone cannot establish a resident-memory saving.

items.statement: Chrome remains portable with unchanged route images and no native dependency.
items.ask: Trace the actual wasm target dependency tree and cfg/feature boundaries: native Apple/Metal crates and apple_tile implementation must be excluded. After T2-CAPTURE M1, retain a pre-change Chrome portable baseline before changing its rendering, then run the full-resolution G3t comparator against the retained pre-change Chrome portable baseline with matching route/content/sample identity; exact scene-linear and submitted SDR output is required. The existing moving command remains smoke proof. Retain the pre-change source revision so the baseline can be reproduced; do not regenerate it with changed output.
items.inspect: Review full-resolution Chrome day/night route frames and 1x motion for Sun, stars, geometry, shadows, mirrors and local lights against its pre-change portable baseline. Native-vs-Chrome coarse-grid agreement alone cannot pass.

items.statement: The iOS simulator selects a truthful recipe from its actual backend facts and draws the valley with its lifecycle lease intact; unsupported simulator facts select portable explicitly.
items.inspect: Boot the iPhone 18 Pro simulator and capture selected recipe/digest and the drawn scene. Verify actual adapter eligibility instead of forcing a hardware claim. Report function only; no physical iPhone performance.

milestones.name: The existing frame lifecycle runs through one split graph
milestones.bar: A production renderer boundary: one owner, prepared fallback, deterministic visible semantics and explicit adverse-case evidence, as in the public wgpu/Metal lifecycle model.

items.statement: Scene and present compile as one graph per generation/variant; scene encoding precedes late acquisition, and an execute-time surface binding gates only present and its dependent epilogue.
items.ask: Inspect graph/executor tests that reject scene work behind acquisition without a surface dependency, require the surface binding only for phase two and prove graph order. At this milestone retain the tone intermediate to isolate the lifecycle change.

items.statement: Healthy acquire refusal flushes uploads without submitting the scene or advancing history; observed loss abandons with no old-queue call; resize/replacement rejects stale generations and retains in-flight resources.
items.ask: Run unchanged-behavior FrameHost/token and real Metal queue-attempt regression witnesses, plus surface byte/letterbox and resize-preparation tests under the merged graph. Require separate healthy refusal, loss-before/after-acquire and successful-submit cases.

items.statement: The merged graph preserves complete image and motion on both native recipes. Same-target scene-linear and submitted SDR bytes remain exact against M0 and paired recipes.
items.inspect: Review the M0 route, cut and skipped-view sequences; compare matching portable/tile checkpoints and accepted-history identities.

items.statement: The iOS foreground lease still refuses an encoded frame raced with backgrounding and resets its histories; replacement resumes from retained world/input state.
items.ask: Run the lease/background race test under merged execution and drive background/foreground plus surface replacement in the simulator. Old-generation callbacks cannot submit or publish.

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: the changed surface path functions in a real Mac game window under both native recipes, including moving input, resize and replacement. This is required functional proof, separate from Mac M2 cadence.
items.inspect: On an unlocked active Mac display, launch the cooked game in a real AppKit window with matching content and recipe identity. Observe presented scene and ordinary control response, resize/letterbox and surface/device replacement recovery; retain window/PID, extent, submission/lifecycle logs and actual window observation evidence. An acquired-format texture or offscreen engine sequence alone cannot prove window presentation. Without a display slot this item stays open; do not waive it as cadence owed.
items.ask: Confirm pre-change Mac motion/cadence evidence is historical. PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 is explicitly rerun after G3t M2/M3 land and uses the post-M3 render path, with no reverse dependency or claim that this functional run proves panel swaps.

milestones.name: Present consumes scene-linear colour directly
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: Present tone-maps and display-encodes one matching scene-linear input/exposure into the surface; the steady Rgba8 intermediate is removed, and logical traffic loses its write/read.
items.ask: Inspect the compiled steady graph, formats and attachment-byte report at a fixed extent. Confirm capture branches remain prepared and never add drawable reads or a second tone operation.

items.statement: Prepared reference-image capture and SDR/sRGB surface/letterbox behavior survive moving tone encoding. Both native recipes preserve exact scene-linear and submitted SDR bytes against the pre-change present oracle.
items.inspect: Review full-resolution route/capture comparisons, surface-format/letterbox witnesses and motion; check exposure correspondence through a cut.
items.ask: Trace the fused shader: does it preserve the old SDR quantization, nearest-source mapping and sRGB decode/attachment encode semantics without allocating the Rgba8 intermediate? Run full-resolution surface-format and letterbox byte witnesses. A new tone curve, shifted sample or arbitrary image tolerance cannot pass.

items.statement: Pass timings are keyed by graph pass name, cover complete executed GPU work and explicitly represent unavailable counters; all native, iOS, browser and capture consumers use the schema.
items.ask: Run timing tests with optional passes absent/present. Trace all FrameSample consumers; fixed positional arrays cannot silently relabel passes. CPU, GPU and callback clocks remain separate.

items.statement: Chrome portable retains route image and execution behavior after the present and timing changes.
items.ask: Run the full-resolution G3t comparator against the retained pre-change Chrome portable baseline, with exact scene-linear/submitted SDR bytes and complete route/sample identity. Trace browser pass-name timing consumers and optional-pass tests; the native-vs-Chrome smoke command cannot establish unchanged output.
items.inspect: Review full-resolution day/night images, letterbox/surface-format witnesses and normal-speed Chrome motion against its own pre-change baseline for missing scene content and exposure/cut errors.

items.statement: ATTENDED SETUP: the changed surface path functions in a real Mac game window under both native recipes, including moving input, resize and replacement. This is required functional proof, separate from Mac M2 cadence.
items.inspect: On an unlocked active Mac display, launch the cooked game in a real AppKit window with matching content and recipe identity. Observe presented scene and ordinary control response, resize/letterbox and surface/device replacement recovery; retain window/PID, extent, submission/lifecycle logs and actual window observation evidence. An acquired-format texture or offscreen engine sequence alone cannot prove window presentation. Without a display slot this item stays open; do not waive it as cadence owed.
items.ask: Confirm pre-change Mac motion/cadence evidence is historical. PLATFORM-RUNTIME-MAC M2 is explicitly rerun after G3t M2/M3 land and uses the post-M3 render path, with no reverse dependency or claim that this functional run proves panel swaps.

milestones.name: Apple slots receive pending changes while portable keeps queue ordering
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: Only Apple pointer-written frame classes receive prepared per-slot buffers/bind groups for instances, directional/local lights, cluster lists and bounds. Portable retains its single queue-ordered buffers and existing dirty tracking; neither recipe creates bind groups in play.
items.ask: Trace forward, shadow, visibility/prepass, transform-history and atmosphere consumers to the selected allocation. Confirm portable uses queue-ordered write_buffer with no added slot copies/cursors, and Apple allocates duplicates only for classes it pointer-writes. Report resident bytes and creation counts per recipe/class.

items.statement: Each Apple slot reconciles accumulated dirtiness from its own last applied generation/sample, including alternating edits, dropped views, refusal/retry, gaps, replay timeline, churn and mapping changes.
items.ask: Run the existing active-prefix/churn and changed-slot/invalid-row GPU tests plus new multi-slot skipped/refused-frame tests. Use distinct values/dirty sets per frame and compare each slot with fresh full preparation; advancing a cursor on an unsuccessful write must fail. Run portable single-buffer dirty/refusal regressions separately; do not impose Apple cursor machinery on portable.

items.statement: The real valley preserves exact same-target scene-linear and submitted SDR bytes through Apple slot reuse and portable queue writes. Upload CPU p50/p95, bytes/ranges, resident copies and deltas against pre-change portable are recorded for both recipes.
items.inspect: Review matched route and changing-row sequences for stale transforms, lights, normals or shadows. Separate upload CPU and GPU time. Include steady dirty motion and full-reconciliation bursts; expose the extra Apple slot propagation and any portable upload-byte increase as a tripwire, with investigation rather than an invented speed gate.

milestones.name: Apple upload transport is safe under completion and fallback
milestones.bar: A production renderer boundary: one owner, prepared fallback, deterministic visible semantics and explicit adverse-case evidence, as in the public wgpu/Metal lifecycle model.

items.statement: The shared-storage candidate imports initialized nonzero buffers from the same Metal device, respects descriptor/usages and writes their CPU pointer only after all prior slot reads complete.
items.ask: Inspect narrowly justified unsafe access and dependency registration. Held-slot tests must fail a pointer write before completion; native storage and imported handles live until generation retirement. Busy slots use counted queue-ordered writes without pointer mutation.

items.statement: Slot churn/refusal/replay tests and the complete valley route match portable under the candidate and forced safe fallback; optional import failure retains a prepared fallback.
items.inspect: Review changing-slot and held-submission witnesses and the route under candidate, forced busy fallback and import rejection. Record validation/errors and fallback reasons.

items.statement: Paired upload CPU, calls and bytes are recorded with A/A controls; the safe shared path has zero write_buffer calls for eligible completed-slot classes. Promote only on measured win with retained quality, validation/admission CPU cost and matched sustained-run thermal evidence required by C12; otherwise record unpromoted candidate and prepared write_buffer fallback.
items.ask: Check warmup, build/extent/load identity, p50/p95, run order and counted busy-slot exceptions. A failed or inconclusive candidate cannot be labelled a selected acceleration, and no allocation/speed threshold is an admission gate. Include per-recipe resident bytes, portable upload-byte delta, fallback CPU work and the design's sustained paired-run duration/start-through-end thermal/power/load records. Missing thermal comparison means unpromoted, not performance-qualified.

milestones.name: Only safely ordered scratch is shared between slots
milestones.bar: A production renderer boundary: one owner, prepared fallback, deterministic visible semantics and explicit adverse-case evidence, as in the public wgpu/Metal lifecycle model.

items.statement: One generation-owned allocation serves each eligible scratch class; histories, retained readbacks, Hi-Z/prepass state and externally retained outputs remain independently owned unless their complete lifetime proves reuse safe.
items.ask: Inspect the complete dependency/lifetime report through final present/capture readers, not only scene encoding. Report eligible subset bytes saved and excluded classes; no claim that total memory halves.

items.statement: A delayed slot plus changing next-slot content and retained capture consumer preserves both outputs without corruption or early retirement; the valley remains exact in same-target scene-linear and submitted SDR bytes.
items.inspect: Inspect the held-submission/capture test output and normal-speed route on both recipes. A deliberately early overwrite must be caught by the witness.

milestones.name: Compact internal rows preserve supplied values and motion
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: A private 128-byte synthetic GPU row preserves affine current transform, prior simulation translation, supplied normals and IDs; public 192-byte InstanceRecord/pack semantics and cooked placement layout remain unchanged.
items.ask: Inspect CPU/WGSL offsets and stride tests, source-to-row decoding and every forward/shadow/prepass/visibility/history/bucket consumer. Test shear/reflection, supplied normals different from inverse transpose and near-singular admitted cases; none may reconstruct or discard supplied normal data.

items.statement: The compact path preserves interpolation, submitted-image history, visibility and upload/refusal semantics against wide-source references.
items.ask: Also run upload/churn and visibility GPU regressions, with skipped and repeated source ticks, cut/reset and recycled identity. A matching current still cannot replace the history witnesses.

items.statement: Both native recipes preserve route image and motion; a 10k row records 1.28 MB instance transport versus 1.92 MB of the old internal row, with all retained history/slot bytes reported.
items.inspect: Review supplied-normal lighting, mirrored and cut/interpolation sequences at native resolution. Compare actual uploads and complete working set, not just an ABI constant.

items.statement: Chrome shaders consume the same private transport and retain the complete route.
items.ask: Trace the actual WebGPU-bound instance buffer and all compiled WGSL consumers to the private 128-byte row, offsets 0/48/60/64/112 and stride 128. Run CPU-to-WGSL decode/stride readbacks on WebGPU with supplied-normal and history witnesses; a Chrome path left on 192-byte rows cannot pass.
items.inspect: Compare full-resolution Chrome route output and normal-speed interpolation/cut/normal-lighting sequences against the retained pre-change portable baseline with exact same-target bytes. The moving command is only smoke proof.

milestones.name: GPU light lists preserve the established lighting choice
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: All named 0/4/16/32/64-light cases must be GPU-qualified on mac-metal, including all-overlap overflow, score-boundary and tie cases; the GPU list builder matches the CPU oracle per cluster, preserving conservative bounds, orthographic intersection, zero intensity, strongest-32 score ranking, index ties, sorted IDs and overflow counts.
items.ask: Run independent CPU-vs-GPU readback tests with all-overlap overflow, score boundaries/ties, camera changes and zero lights. CPU uploads only per-source data, not completed dense lists. F32 ranking disagreements select the prepared CPU path with a reason and cannot count as GPU-qualified cases. Every named case must execute the GPU builder and match exact oracle readbacks; CPU fallback leaves this item unsatisfied. If overflow cannot qualify, keep M8 open and re-plan rather than treating a subset as completion.

items.statement: Both recipes preserve dense local-light images and normal-speed motion; record GPU binning/forward time, CPU bounds/validation/admission/fallback and full-frame cost, overflow, allocations and fallback counts from 4 through 64 lights.
items.inspect: Review near/far lit receivers and saturated clusters during the camera route. Reject missing strongest lights or flicker hidden by a global image metric. Report all fallback work and departures from the bounded top-32 cost model. Require exact same-target pre-blend HDR/SDR comparisons and membership readbacks, not a perceptual allowance for missing weak lights.

items.statement: The portable Chrome light path preserves the same overflow semantics and visible lighting.
items.ask: Run the light-list/readback and dense-light scene witnesses on WebGPU. Record GPU vs CPU fallback explicitly and compare to its own portable CPU oracle.

milestones.name: Mirrored ranges preserve existing visibility ownership
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: M9 delivers one V2-owned class/range mechanism using existing determinant/membership state, shared by supported draw paths and the private bucket consumer. All camera/prepass/shadow consumers preserve their admitted raster policy and established direct order; no experimental mixed-mesh promotion is implied.
items.ask: Trace upload, shared classifier/range layout, buckets, mesh_route, visibility, forward and shadow consumers: no second determinant/class/range authority may remain. Preserve legacy scene-wide cull-none for its affected order group; open/unknown, explicitly two-sided and near-singular meshes stay two-sided. Closure alone cannot narrow legacy semantics. Opposite front-face culling is limited to already admitted one-sided semantics. Supported legacy ranges preserve physical-slot order using stable runs; private buckets keep their existing oracle order. Test empty runs, churn and determinant boundaries, and record V2/G3c source/contract review in the independent M9 verdict. Coalesce adjacent equal raster states across facing signs so legacy two-sided groups do not incur one draw per sign run.

items.statement: Synthetic mirror overlay slot 5060, open/back-side/interior fixtures, equal-depth ties and off-camera casters preserve exact colour/depth against supported pre-change and corresponding direct oracles on both recipes.
items.inspect: Review near-surface, open single-sided geometry viewed from both sides, unknown closure, interior views, cut and shadow sequences. Verify cooked negative winding is baked and is not the runtime mirror fixture. Wrongly back-culling a required two-sided range must fail; cull-none must fail the pipeline-state assertion only for an admitted one-sided witness. Inspect output and direct ordering, not just facing labels.

items.statement: CPU range-maintenance cost, draws and complete GPU work are recorded at zero and 1/11 mirrored instances, by occupied stable run/bucket and admitted raster policy.
items.ask: Compare supported direct/frustum/occlusion and count ordinary, mirrored and two-sided runs separately, including interleaved signs and order-sensitive ties. Report extra stable-run draws and any lack of culling win honestly; no universal +1 draw or benefit from unqualified buckets.

milestones.name: A stateful native segment composes inside one submission
milestones.bar: A production renderer boundary: one owner, prepared fallback, deterministic visible semantics and explicit adverse-case evidence, as in the public wgpu/Metal lifecycle model.

items.statement: After independent review of C06/the boundary, graph-declared native work uses a dedicated whole raw encoder between wgpu encoders in one ordered coordinator submit, with no surface import or mixed recording.
items.ask: Inspect graph hazards and refusal tests, locked-wgpu encoder API separation, one queue and error paths. Native-written resources are initialized through wgpu, never aliased/discarded and retained by the generation.

items.statement: A labelled native storage-writing scene-HDR/history blend matches its prepared wgpu twin within 1 ULP f16/channel across the route, reset and replacement; it is composition proof, not MetalFX or a tile speed claim.
items.inspect: Compare same-submit visible output, history across frames and forced portable rejection at full resolution. Inspect source and output readbacks so a no-op native segment or hidden wgpu producer cannot pass.

items.statement: Held submission and generation replacement retain native textures/provider until completion; encoded-but-discarded or failed frames reset internal history before reuse, with outcome counters.
items.ask: Run same-submit, held-slot, acquire-refusal, cut, extent replacement, loss and submission-failure witnesses. Preserve healthy flush vs lost-device abandon. Do not add submit-without-present to avoid a reset.

items.statement: An encoded native frame raced with iOS backgrounding is refused by the platform lease and resets provider history; no background submission occurs.
items.ask: Run the raced native-frame lease test and simulator background/resume witness; report function only and retain world/input state.

milestones.name: Native providers survive replacement and expose truthful timing
milestones.bar: A production renderer boundary: one owner, prepared fallback, deterministic visible semantics and explicit adverse-case evidence, as in the public wgpu/Metal lifecycle model.

items.statement: Provider extent/generation replacements prepare off the render critical path with a ready twin, publish through existing generation admission and retire only on completion; no pipeline/native-object creation occurs in play.
items.ask: Use bounded provider extent fixtures and existing replacement runtime, without waiting for G4 real scale transitions. Confirm old/new overlap is accounted, failed preparation leaves the live provider intact and stale completion cannot publish.

items.statement: Forced provider rejection, surface replacement, command-buffer error and device loss select the correct prepared fallback/rebuild and reset history without old-generation queue work.
items.inspect: Review failure/recovery route output and event order against the uninterrupted same-build control. Device-loss errors must reach the platform generation owner; provider rejection alone is not device loss.

items.statement: Native segment GPU start/end appears under the matching pass identity only after completion, is nonzero and correctly related to its submission; missing timing is explicit.
items.ask: Run timing/completion tests and inspect one actual native segment row. Distinguish Metal and wgpu clock domains; compare spans only with a documented correlation, never assume absolute clocks coincide.

milestones.name: An integrated record states qualified wins and remaining targets
milestones.bar: The same complete cooked valley as portable, with stable lighting, silhouettes, shadows and motion expected of a shipped high-end game; matched full-resolution stills and normal-speed sequences must expose omitted work.

items.statement: Paired Apple/portable route rows record full GPU/pass/native times, upload/encode CPU, creation/allocation/retirement, logical bytes and registry digest at fixed extents 1280x720 and 1920x1080, with A/A and alternating runs. The integrated scaling row also runs the representative 10,000-entity field with 1,000–2,000 movers and full/partial visibility through existing supported draw paths. Record validation/admission and CPU-fallback work, resident selected/fallback/variant totals, portable upload-byte deltas and a sustained paired run with actual duration and thermal state at start/throughout/end.
items.ask: Review source/shader/route/cooked hashes, warmup/load, p50/p95, fallback counts and end-of-window outstanding work. No new G4 dynamic scaling/reconstruction or physical cadence claim follows from these fixed extents. Check the design's at-least-ten-minute-per-recipe sustained window after warmup (method, not a numeric performance gate), power/load, thermal sampling and throttling. Confounded/unavailable thermal comparisons cannot qualify promotion. Account every unique fallback allocation and generation overlap; include all validation/admission/oracle work in complete CPU cost.

items.statement: Eligibility and one-off mechanism ablations identify actual readers and the selected paths at the shipped configuration, with comparable win/no measurable effect/unpromoted conclusions and assigned tripwire follow-up. Any promoted path requires preserved quality, full validation/fallback costs and comparable sustained-run thermal evidence; otherwise it remains unpromoted.
items.ask: Check M1/M3-M9 mechanisms, complete stage costs, excluded scratch and later readers. Keep physical replay bytes separate and unmeasured where no new replay exists. Native provider is still a stand-in until G4 qualifies MetalFX. Reconcile D12.1 thermal/duration, resident fallback bytes and validation/admission CPU costs with each win claim. Missing or confounded sustained thermal evidence cannot be called performance-qualified; no numeric budget is invented.

items.statement: The integrated native game preserves required image and normal-speed motion on both recipes and records cadence/physical-device qualifications still owed without claiming Mac M2 closure.
items.inspect: Review full-resolution matched checkpoint and motion sets including cut, night, local lights, mirrors, skipped views and fallback/recovery. Read all module source changes against C04/C06/C07/C08/C12 and the brief; no omitted consumer can be waived by this item. Confirm D2.5/D3.5 actual Mac window runs passed and the final assembly has a functional window smoke run on both recipes. Functional window presentation cannot be recorded as owed to close G3t; only cadence and physical-device qualification can remain owed. Mac M2 must rerun the post-M3 path.

items.statement: Chrome portable passes the integrated moving route and retains lighting/visibility/present semantics.
items.ask: Run WebGPU dense-light readbacks against the CPU oracle including 32/64 all-overlap overflow/ties, and visibility direct/frustum/occlusion membership/order witnesses where supported. Trace actual 128-byte shader bindings, graph timing and present consumers. Compare complete full-resolution output to the retained pre-change Chrome portable baseline under the mechanism-specific contract; native-vs-Chrome coarse-grid parity cannot pass a shared omission.
items.inspect: Review native-size Chrome noon/night checkpoints and 1x route/cut/mirror/lighting sequences against its pre-change baseline. Require the one-light, one-mirrored-cube and night-star negative controls to fail; account every route sample and any fallback.

items.statement: The simulator runs the integrated recipe/fallback with lifecycle recovery, while physical iPhone speed/loss and real Mac display rows remain explicitly unqualified.
items.inspect: Boot and drive integrated background/foreground, rotation and replacement, capture the scene and recipe/fallback identity. Label simulator function and any Mac proxy separately from physical device results.

items.statement: The final integrated revision passes required repository checks and its evidence/ledger records separate implementation, correctness, visual and device status.
items.ask: Confirm the final diff/evidence is the checked revision, optional creation diagnostics and browser/simulator paths were exercised where affected, and no speed claim or maturity promotion is inferred from repository checks alone.
